norms.text: The shed names are said in order after a shift.
A family sleeps where its hand on the roll can see it from the barge.

taboos.text: Asking a hand when the debt will end.

values.text: The clutch, which is the reason the families stay.

contempts.text: The overseers' habit of counting the families' food against the debt.

people.text: Families who stand by each other's hands.

faction.text: The house adds to the debt faster than the gang can work it.

addressTerms.text: By name among themselves; walker to strangers.

neverSaid.text: That the families should leave the clutch. Two break this on purpose. Finds-The-Other-Bank would take the families to the port. Ri'Sakka is counted a hand and never kin, so the clutch does not hold him.

grievances.text: Food, sickness and broken tools are added to the gang's debt.

views.text: They walk the doors at dusk and write down who is late.
